advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make epoch_for_position compare positions using the same integer HLC ordering as reducer/_sort.event_sort_key rather than a lexical string `<`.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:212: `if _position_prefix(base) < event_position:`
reducer/_sort.py:20-25 `prefix_ts` returns `int(seg)` and compares as integer; module docstring: 'string comparison only agrees while every name has the *same* width'

epoch_for_position claims the epoch is 'the identity's keyring_epoch cursor value as of that position' derived from 'HLC filename order', but uses a lexical `<` compare that does not match the integer fold order
advisory.finding: epoch_for_position compares event-filename position prefixes with lexical string comparison (`_position_prefix(base) < event_position`), but the reducer's canonical fold order compares the HLC timestamp prefix as an INTEGER (reducer/_sort.py prefix_ts). Mixed-width timestamp names (legacy 19-digit ns vs HLC) sort differently under string vs integer comparison, so the epoch step count can diverge from the true fold position — the function may return the wrong epoch and select the wrong epoch-scoped trust root.
scenarios: An identity whose event log mixes legacy 19-digit-ns and shorter/longer HLC filename prefixes
Any KEY event whose timestamp digit-width differs from event_position's width
advisory.suggested_fix: Compare using the integer timestamp prefix (and the shared event_sort_key/prefix_ts comparator) instead of `_position_prefix(base) < event_position`, so epoch counting matches the canonical fold order across mixed-width filenames.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and enforce whether a fully-revoked identity may be re-TOFU'd; if not, gate genesis on 'the keyring has never held a key' rather than 'no currently-valid keys'.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:261: `is_genesis = not (state.get("keys") or [])`
reducer/_processors.py:53-63 `_rederive_keyring_keys` sets `state['keys'] = keys_valid_at_epoch(...)`, which is empty once every record has a revoked_epoch
docstring at identity.py:250 says genesis is 'when the identity currently has NO valid keys' — which is also true after full revocation, not only at true first use
`is_genesis = not (state.get("keys") or [])` and when genesis, no signature is required (src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:261-265)
`revoke_identity_key` places no floor on remaining valid keys; it revokes any currently-valid matching key (src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:275-300)
`_rederive_keyring_keys` yields `state['keys'] == []` once all records are revoked at the latest epoch (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:53-63)
advisory.finding: An identity whose keys have ALL been revoked reverts to state['keys']==[] , so add_identity_key's genesis test `is_genesis = not (state.get('keys') or [])` treats the next KEY_ADD as an unsigned trust-on-first-use genesis. Any actor can then re-seed the keyring of a fully-revoked identity without any signature from a previously-valid key.
merged_from: A signed KEY_REVOKE of the last currently-valid key leaves the identity keyless, after which `add_identity_key` treats the next KEY_ADD as an unsigned TOFU genesis (`is_genesis = not (state.get('keys') or [])`). This lets a revoke chain reset an identity to an unauthenticated genesis state, allowing an unsigned key to (re)take control.
scenarios: Revoke the sole/last valid key of an identity, then a third party calls add_identity_key with signature=None

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unreachable RETIRED_SUFFIX stripping in epoch_for_position (files are pre-filtered by is_active_event) or clarify the intent.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:181: listing filters `... and is_active_event(f)` (excludes *.retired)
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:203: `base = os.path.basename(path).removesuffix(RETIRED_SUFFIX)` operates only on already-active names
advisory.finding: epoch_for_position applies `removesuffix(RETIRED_SUFFIX)` to filenames it already excluded via `is_active_event(f)`, so the retired-suffix stripping is dead code and the comment 'compacted KEY events before it are retired... must NOT be re-scanned' does not correspond to any live path here.
scenarios: Reading the function to reason about snapshot/retired handling

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (or reject) KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE signatures inside the reducer/verification path, not only in the write-gate, so a forged/synced KEY event cannot inject a trust-root key.
evidence: `process_key_event` reads only `public_key = data.get("public_key")` and never inspects `data['signature']` before appending `{"public_key": public_key, "added_epoch": cursor, ...}` to the keyring (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:83-88)

`_rederive_keyring_keys` sets `state['keys'] = keys_valid_at_epoch(keyring, epoch)` so the keyring directly becomes the authorship trust root consumed by `resolve_trust_root`/`verify_authorship` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:53-63, authorship.py:93-96)
The write-gate is the ONLY place a signature is checked: `_verify_keyop_signature(...)` in add/revoke, not in the reducer (src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:211-238, 263-265)

The held-out test writes a raw KEY_ADD event with `"signature": None` and `"author": "adversary"` directly into the ticket dir and asserts the reducer adds pub3 to the keyring (`rec['added_epoch'] == 2`) — proving the reducer does not require a valid signature (tests/unit/test_identity_e165_heldout.py:171-197)

rebar is a merge/sync distributed store: SCHEMA_VERSION notes describe an older clone preserving foreign KEY events until upgrade, and a SYNC bridge exists (src/rebar/reducer/_version.py comment; event_append EVENT_TYPES includes SYNC), so events cross a trust boundary the write-gate does not own
advisory.finding: The reducer folds KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE events into the identity keyring (which becomes the authorship trust root via `_rederive_keyring_keys` -> `state['keys']`) WITHOUT verifying the signature stored on the event. Signature authorization is enforced ONLY in the write-gate `_verify_keyop_signature`; any KEY_ADD reaching the event store by another path (raw file, cross-clone sync/merge, forged SNAPSHOT) injects an attacker key into the trust root with no valid signature.
scenarios: An attacker with write access to a clone (or via a synced/merged branch) drops a `{ts}-{uuid}-KEY_ADD.json` naming their own public key with `signature: null`; after reduce, their key is a currently-valid authorship key for the victim identity and can forge authorship attestations.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for `epoch_for_position` covering the no-snapshot, post-snapshot-step, and snapshot-base cases.
evidence: `def epoch_for_position(identity_id: str, event_position: str, *, repo_root=None) -> int:` at authorship.py:159
search for `epoch_for_position` returns only the definition site — no test file references it
The function has non-trivial branches (snapshot base_epoch read at lines 191-197, post-snapshot step counting at 200-213) none of which are exercised
advisory.finding: New public function `epoch_for_position` (snapshot-aware epoch computation: reads a SNAPSHOT's frozen keyring_epoch as base, then counts post-snapshot KEY events whose filename sorts before the target position) has no test at all. A regression in the base-epoch read, the snap_idx start slice, the KEY-event-type filter, or the `_position_prefix < event_position` comparison would pass CI silently.
scenarios: A snapshot exists and epoch base must be read from compiled_state
Post-snapshot KEY events before/after the target position

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a signature over a different op/identity/public_key is refused (payload-mismatch replay guard).
evidence: `expected = authorship.keyop_payload(op, identity_id, public_key)` / `if signature.payload != expected:` at identity.py:227-231
test_identity_e165_heldout.py `_sign_keyop` always signs the exact matching op/identity/pubkey (lines 71-74), so the payload-mismatch branch never executes
No test asserts a replayed signature (e.g. a KEY_ADD signature reused for KEY_REVOKE, or a signature for a different pubkey) is refused
`verdict = authorship.verify_authorship(signature, identity_id, repo_root=repo_root)` / `if not verdict.verified:` at identity.py:233-238
test_unsigned_rotation_refused passes signature=None (identity.py path raises before verify_authorship); test_signed_rotation_accepted signs with the valid genesis key
No test signs a KEY_ADD payload with an outsider/revoked private key and asserts the add is refused with no event appended
advisory.finding: The anti-replay payload-mismatch guard is untested: `_verify_keyop_signature` refuses a signature whose `.payload` does not exactly equal `keyop_payload(op, identity_id, public_key)` (docstring: 'a signature over some other op / identity / key can't be replayed here'). No test supplies a validly-signed envelope over a DIFFERENT op/identity/key to assert the rotation is refused. The held-out suite covers only unsigned refusal and correctly-signed acceptance.
merged_from: Rejection of a rotation signed by a key that is NOT currently valid (outsider key, or a revoked key) is untested. The gate's `if not verdict.verified` branch is only reached via the unsigned path; no test signs a rotation over the correct payload using a key that is not in the identity's currently-valid keyring and asserts refusal.
scenarios: An attacker replays a valid signature captured for one key-op to authorize a different key-op

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `create_identity(..., keys=[pub])` seeds a keyring at added_epoch 0 with keyring_epoch 1, and that a signed rotation off that seeded key is accepted.
evidence: `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` seeds keyring from `state.get('keys')` at _processors.py:105-121, called from process_create (line 216) and process_snapshot migration (line 796)
In test_identity_e165*.py every identity is created via `create_identity('Ada','ada@example.com', ...)` with no keys= argument, then TOFU-added (e.g. e165.py:61, heldout.py:66)
No e165 test creates an identity with keys= to assert the CREATE-seeded keyring lands at epoch 0 with keyring_epoch 1
advisory.finding: The genesis-bootstrap-from-CREATE path (`_bootstrap_genesis_keyring`) is not exercised by the e165 tests: an identity created with a static `keys` list (`create_identity(..., keys=[pub])`) should seed one epoch-0 keyring record per key with cursor->1. All e165 tests use the keyless identity + TOFU KEY_ADD path instead.
scenarios: An identity created with keys at creation time (the ddbe path) then does a signed rotation relying on the seeded epoch-0 key
